archetypes.name: shell-parity
archetypes.rationale: The plan claims parity with ci-wait.sh, ci-decide.sh, ci-failed-jobs.sh, ci-rerun-failed.sh, gh-run-logs.sh, and run_evaluate_failure in ship-pr.sh; any wrong constant, missing decision-matrix cell, or mis-mapped sentinel silently mis-routes CI.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read the plan's claimed parity against each source shell script: ci-wait.sh (poll loop, suspend-window exemption, 3-consecutive-failure bail, NO_CHECKS handling), ci-decide.sh (all matrix rows including the merge-past-cap allowance and exact iteration/rebase/fix_attempt cap values), ci-failed-jobs.sh (fixable job list membership, shard parse form, malformed-name handling), ci-rerun-failed.sh (already_running detection logic), gh-run-logs.sh (100-line tail constant, rc=3 in-progress defer), and run_evaluate_failure in ship-pr.sh (transient_retries<1 rerun-only path, fix-loop cap of 3, backoff shape). For each shell source, compare the exact constant values, exit-code semantics, and branch conditions stated in the plan against the actual script content; flag any divergence, missing branch, or wrong sentinel. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: phase1-contract
archetypes.rationale: The plan is blocked-by Phase 1 and calls specific symbols on gh.py, git.py, agents.py, redact.py, outcomes.py, retry.py, errors.py, and proc.py; if any called symbol is absent or carries a different signature, the plan cannot be executed without unplanned edits to those files.
archetypes.prompt_body: For every Phase-1 symbol the plan invokes — gh.pr_view, gh.failed_jobs, gh.run_rerun, gh.run_view, git.rev_parse, git.rev_count, git.merge_base, git.push, git.reset, agents.run_waterfall, agents.launch_tier, agents.classify_launch_failure, agents.is_transient_infra_failure, redact.redact, outcomes.Outcome, outcomes.StepResult, and the proc.Runner interface — read the actual Phase-1 source files under python/ and verify that each symbol exists with the parameter contract and return type the plan assumes. Flag any symbol that is absent, renamed, or has a different signature, and flag any Runner argv-keying or return-type assumption that diverges from the actual implementation. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
